outputs.L3:
The system includes a computer-controlled goods-to-person picking station for processing picking orders from storage containers. At the picking station, storage containers containing the required articles are brought to an operator or automated picking device so that the articles can be removed efficiently.

During operation, selected articles are picked from the storage containers into conveyor bags. These conveyor bags are then transported by a suspension conveyor to a packing location, where the articles assigned to a particular picking order are consolidated and packed.

In addition, the system includes an order container conveyor for transporting order containers, such as boxes, totes, or other shipping containers, that are assigned to specific picking orders. These order containers may receive articles directly during the picking process when appropriate.

The computer coordinates the overall picking and transport process. It determines, for each picking order, which articles are to be picked directly into an assigned order container and which articles are to be picked into conveyor bags for later use in fulfilling current or future orders. By making this distinction, the system can improve picking efficiency, support order consolidation, and ensure that articles are delivered to the packing location in the correct sequence for completion of the picking orders.
outputs.L4:
A computerized goods-to-person picking system is designed to fulfill customer orders efficiently by bringing required inventory items to a picking station rather than requiring workers to travel through warehouse aisles to locate products. In this type of system, storage containers holding various goods are automatically retrieved from a storage area and delivered to a picking station under the control of a warehouse management or control system. The system identifies which items are needed for active orders, presents the appropriate storage containers to an operator or robotic picker, and provides instructions indicating which products and quantities should be removed.

At the picking station, selected items are taken from the storage containers and placed into designated receiving containers. In some cases, the items are placed directly into order containers, such as totes or boxes, that are assigned to a specific customer order and can later be sent to packing or shipping. In other cases, the items are placed into conveyor bags or similar transport carriers. These bags may be used when the picked items are intended for orders that will be completed at a later stage, combined with other items from different picking zones, or temporarily routed through the facility before final packing.

Once items have been picked, the system uses conveyors and related transport mechanisms to move the filled order containers, bags, or boxes away from the picking station. Conveyor bags may be routed to buffering, sorting, consolidation, or packing areas, depending on the status of the associated orders. Completed order containers can be sent directly to a packing location, while partially completed orders can be held or redirected until all required items have been collected. The computerized control system tracks the identity and location of each container or bag throughout the process, ensuring that picked items are correctly associated with their corresponding orders.

This arrangement allows the system to fulfill a first order immediately when all required items are available and can be placed directly into a dedicated order container. At the same time, the picker can continue selecting additional items from the same storage container for other orders and place those items into conveyor bags for later processing. By allowing multiple orders to be served during a single presentation of a storage container, the system reduces the number of container retrievals, minimizes idle time at the picking station, and increases overall picking productivity.

The use of conveyor bags also adds flexibility to order handling. Items for later orders do not need to wait until a complete order container is present at the picking station. Instead, they can be picked opportunistically, transported through the conveyor system, and combined with other order components when appropriate. This improves the ability of the warehouse to manage varying order priorities, batch picking operations, and different fulfillment workflows. As a result, the computerized goods-to-person system supports both rapid fulfillment of immediately completable orders and efficient preparation of items for future or partially completed orders, thereby improving throughput, accuracy, and operational flexibility.
outputs.L5:
**Selected**

The word **“selected”** suggests something chosen with care, attention, and purpose. When something is selected, it is not random; it has been considered and picked because it meets certain standards or fits a specific need. Selection can apply to many areas of life, from choosing the right book to read, selecting the best candidate for a job, or picking high-quality products from a larger group.

Being selected often carries a sense of value and recognition. For example, a student selected for an award may feel proud because their hard work has been noticed. A product labeled as “selected” may suggest quality, exclusivity, or special attention to detail. In this way, selection helps people identify what is most suitable, meaningful, or excellent.

However, selection also requires responsibility. Making a good choice means understanding the purpose, comparing options, and thinking about the outcome. Whether in business, education, art, or everyday life, the act of selecting shapes decisions and influences results.

In short, **selected** means more than simply chosen. It represents intention, quality, and thoughtful decision-making.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize this patent claim in one paragraph, keeping the technical terms: a goods-to-person picking system with storage containers, order containers, conveyor bags, a suspension conveyor, packing location, and computer-controlled picking orders.
counterfactuals.output: The patent claim describes a goods-to-person picking system in which storage containers holding goods, order containers assigned to customer orders, and conveyor bags are coordinated to fulfill computer-controlled picking orders. A suspension conveyor transports the conveyor bags and/or containers through the system, while goods are picked from storage containers into order containers according to the picking orders. The order containers are then conveyed to a packing location, where the completed orders are prepared for shipment.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an automated warehouse picking method where articles are picked from storage containers into both order boxes and conveyor bags, and the conveyor bags are later transported to packing for completing orders.
counterfactuals.output: An automated warehouse picking method is disclosed in which articles are retrieved from storage containers and selectively allocated to a plurality of fulfillment receptacles including order boxes and conveyor bags. A control system receives order data, identifies required articles, and directs delivery of storage containers to one or more picking stations. At the picking stations, articles are removed from the storage containers and placed either directly into order boxes associated with customer orders or into conveyor bags assigned to orders or order portions. The conveyor bags are conveyed from the picking stations to a downstream packing area, where the articles contained in the conveyor bags are combined with corresponding order boxes and/or additional articles to complete the customer orders. The method enables mixed receptacle picking, decouples article retrieval from final packing, and improves throughput and flexibility in automated order fulfillment operations.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe the invention in formal patent language: a computer-controlled picking station using the good-to-person principle, conveyor bags on a suspension conveyor, and order containers on a separate conveyor, where some items are picked immediately and others are buffered for later orders.
counterfactuals.output:
A computer-controlled picking station is provided for order fulfillment according to a goods-to-person principle. The picking station comprises a suspension conveyor configured to transport a plurality of conveyor bags, each conveyor bag being adapted to contain one or more items, and a separate container conveyor configured to transport a plurality of order containers to and from a picking position. The picking station further comprises at least one control unit operatively connected to the suspension conveyor, the container conveyor, and an operator interface, the control unit being configured to coordinate the arrival of conveyor bags and order containers at the picking station in accordance with stored order data.

In operation, the control unit causes a conveyor bag containing at least one item required for an active order to be delivered by the suspension conveyor to the picking station and causes an order container assigned to the active order to be delivered by the container conveyor to a corresponding dispensing or loading position. An operator, or an automated handling device, removes a required item from the conveyor bag and deposits the item into the order container in response to instructions generated by the control unit.

The picking station is further configured to distinguish between items required for an order currently present at the picking station and items not immediately required for such order. Items removed from a conveyor bag that are required for an active order are transferred directly into the respective order container. Items removed from the conveyor bag that are not required for an order container currently present at the picking station are transferred to a buffer location associated with the picking station. The buffer location may comprise a temporary storage receptacle, shelf, compartment, auxiliary container, or buffer conveyor configured to hold the buffered items under control of the control unit.

The control unit maintains data associating each buffered item with at least one subsequent order. When an order container for a subsequent order requiring a buffered item is delivered to the picking station or to a downstream picking position, the control unit issues an instruction to retrieve the buffered item from the buffer location and transfer the buffered item into the corresponding order container. In this manner, the picking station enables immediate picking of items for current orders while also permitting pre-picking or intermediate storage of items for later orders, thereby improving utilization of conveyor bag presentations, reducing repeated transport of the same stock units, and increasing throughput of the order fulfillment system.

In one embodiment, the suspension conveyor conveys the conveyor bags independently of the order containers, such that arrival of the conveyor bags and order containers may be controlled separately. The conveyor bags may be suspended from carriers movable along an overhead rail system, and the order containers may be moved on a belt conveyor, roller conveyor, chain conveyor, shuttle conveyor, or other floor-based conveying device. The control unit may determine, based on order data and item availability, whether an item presented in a conveyor bag is to be picked immediately into an order container or transferred to the buffer for later completion of another order.

Accordingly, the invention relates to a method and apparatus for operating a goods-to-person picking station in which conveyor bags are supplied by a suspension conveyor and order containers are supplied by a separate conveyor, wherein presented items are selectively either picked directly into order containers for active orders or buffered under computer control for subsequent transfer into order containers of later orders.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
